issues.source_quote: Отдуплились. Знай наших. Есть такая.
issues.translation_quote: Doubled out. That's how we do it. Got one.
issues.justification: This is a domino scene (отдуплиться = play off a double, 'Есть такая' = I have that tile). 'Doubled out' and 'Got one' obscure the game and are unclear in English.

issues.source_quote: Рыба!
issues.translation_quote: Fish!
issues.justification: In dominoes 'рыба' is the blocked-game term (a 'fish', i.e., a draw/block); rendered literally with no context, it reads as nonsense.

issues.source_quote: Я то свою меру отлично знаю. А вот вас, вас я давно наблюдаю!
issues.translation_quote: I'll ask you to spare me your familiarity! I know my limit perfectly well.
issues.justification: Velyurov's drunken indignation is rendered stiffly; also 'Мотылек! Мне грустно, но вы приняли допинг' is garbled, losing the sense that Kostik is accused of being intoxicated/excited.

issues.source_quote: Лежала холодная братцы война.
issues.translation_quote: There lay the Cold War, brothers.
issues.justification: Soyev's parody lyric (a parody of a thieves' song about a corpse under the seat) is changed by adding 'Cold War', an invented anachronistic specification; the verse also loses its rhyme and comic ineptitude.

issues.source_quote: Хотите по гамбургскому счету?
issues.translation_quote: Want to judge by the true measure?
issues.justification: 'По гамбургскому счету' is an idiom for honest, unvarnished assessment; 'true measure' is vague and the next line repeats it awkwardly, losing the idiom.

issues.source_quote: Роза Муда - шент мир дер херц унд дер я. Роза Муда - франк ду них мерт ди мама.
issues.translation_quote: Rosa Muda - schenk mir dein Herz und sag ja. Rosa Muda - frag doch nicht mehr die Mama.
issues.justification: The source is deliberately pseudo-German gibberish (the song's nonsense lines); the translator 'corrected' it into real German, altering the joke. Also the earlier 'Роза Муда' lines are rendered into semi-sensible English that changes the intended nonsense.

issues.source_quote: Эсси тью травайе!
issues.translation_quote: Essaie de travailler!
issues.justification: Source gibberish-French spelling is silently normalized; and 'Ву зет ридикюль' / 'Се монифик' are similarly corrected, losing Margarita's mangled-foreign-phrase characterization.

issues.source_quote: Ауфвидеркукен.
issues.translation_quote: Auf Wiederkucken.
issues.justification: The joke is a Russian-German hybrid pun (ауфвидерзен + кукен); the transliteration back to German-looking text doesn't convey it.

issues.source_quote: Нет, она не то, чтоб уехала, а просто ушла.
issues.translation_quote: No, she didn't exactly go away, she simply left.
issues.justification: The distinction between 'уехала' (travelled away) and 'ушла' (left him) is lost: 'go away' and 'left' are nearly synonymous in English, killing the euphemistic point.

issues.source_quote: Вы прекрасно кололи.
issues.translation_quote: You gave wonderful injections.
issues.justification: The comic double entendre of the injection/love-scene dialogue is weakened; 'Lyudochka' dialogue also loses 'Один раз... На прощание' tone; 'I felt a great deal' is stilted.

issues.source_quote: Живописцы, окуните ваши кисти
issues.translation_quote: Painters, dip your brushes
issues.justification: The song lyrics lose rhyme, rhythm and singability entirely; 'Arbat' songs are poetry, rendered as flat prose, and 'словно листья к ноябрю' becomes the odd 'by November'.

issues.source_quote: Был я конкурсе я джазов, обалдел от джазов сразу. Буги-вуги, самба-мамба, чувствую, приходит амба.
issues.translation_quote: Went to a jazz contest, man, the jazz just knocked me flat. Boogie-woogie, samba-mamba, I'm a goner, that is that.
issues.justification: Soyev's intentionally clumsy parody verse (the 'я джазов' grammatical error is the joke) is smoothed into slick American slang ('man'), losing the satire.

issues.source_quote: Тунеядца хоронили, плакали подруги... А два джаза на могиле дули: буги, вуги...
issues.translation_quote: They buried a freeloader, his girlfriends wept... And two jazz bands at the grave blew: boogie, woogie...
issues.justification: 'Тунеядец' was a specific Soviet legal/ideological label ('parasite'); 'freeloader' is casual, and the verse loses its rhyme.

issues.source_quote: Нынче цирк без зазывал! Всю Москву сюда зазвал!
issues.translation_quote: Today the circus needs no barkers! It's called all of Moscow here!
issues.justification: The wordplay on зазывал/зазвал (and the circus-market rhyme) is lost; the following 'рынок к нам пристроили' becomes confusing.

issues.source_quote: Я - кандидат в мастера Вы - кандидат? Вы давно уже мастер.
issues.translation_quote: I'm a candidate master. You, a candidate? You've long been a master.
issues.justification: The pun on chess rank vs. 'master' of seduction is weakly rendered; 'Ох, вы и мастер' loses its innuendo, and 'candidate's exams' later confuses two senses of 'кандидатский'.

issues.source_quote: Это какой-то палеолит!
issues.translation_quote: This is some kind of Paleolithic!
issues.justification: Unnatural calque; 'This is the Stone Age!' would be idiomatic.

issues.source_quote: Вы - служитель муз. Я служу "Мосэстраде".
issues.translation_quote: You're a servant of the muses. I serve "Mosestrada."
issues.justification: The comic deflation survives but 'Мосэстрада' is never glossed; more importantly 'Мон папа, не же па' (a deliberately garbled French lyric) is rendered as correct 'ne veut pas', losing the garble and the 'Нё жё па?' joke.

issues.source_quote: Хоботов, не галди.
issues.translation_quote: Khobotov, stop squawking.
issues.justification: Oddly avian register; 'галдеть' means to make a racket. Also 'Анфант террибль, несчастный' / 'Ты в шорах' are rendered awkwardly ('blinkers' is British, mixing with American 'apartment').

issues.source_quote: Вот дает.
issues.translation_quote: He's something.
issues.justification: Weak rendering of colloquial admiration/surprise; later 'Вот дает!' as 'Wow!' and 'Вот чумовой!' as 'What a nutcase!' are inconsistent.

issues.source_quote: Вот уж и осень, скоро дожди пойдут... Самое гриппозное время.
issues.translation_quote: Whatever he writes - "it's matchless!" It's all his wife.
issues.justification: Soyev's wife's flattery pattern is only dimly conveyed; 'Что не напишет - все бесподобно' should read as the wife's reaction, quote marks make this ambiguous.

issues.source_quote: Он сомнителен... Я бы ему не доверял.
issues.translation_quote: He's dubious... He's dubious. I wouldn't trust him.
issues.justification: Fine, but 'Торгуете телом?' rendered 'You sell your body?' misses the pun on 'создаю людям новые торсы' (selling torsos) and sounds crude.

issues.source_quote: Тоже нашел себе дурочку с переулочка.
issues.translation_quote: Found yourself a little fool from down the lane, did you.
issues.justification: The idiom (a dumb girl off the street) is rendered in a literal, unnatural way.

issues.source_quote: - Схожу ума. - Здорово.
issues.translation_quote: "Going out of mind." - Cool.
issues.justification: Anachronistic slang 'Cool' for 1950s dialogue; the telegram's archaic phrase 'схожу с ума' is mangled.

issues.source_quote: Вы - как дитя. А между тем, мне уже 43 года. И направление где-то посеяли.
issues.translation_quote: You're like a child. And meanwhile, I'm already 43. And you lost your referral somewhere.
issues.justification: Mistranslation: the referral was lost by Khobotov himself ('И направление где-то посеяли' is impersonal, not 'you'), and attribution of speakers is muddled.

issues.source_quote: Ну, кой черт, занес вас на эти галеры?
issues.translation_quote: So what the devil brought you to these galleys?
issues.justification: Literal, loses the Molière allusion naturalness; acceptable but stiff. Also 'Hello. - A slight bruise.' misassigns lines.

issues.source_quote: Взял Ромео для Джульеты в магазине две котлеты.
issues.translation_quote: Romeo bought for Juliet two cutlets at the store. They both ate up those cutlets - Romeo and Juliet are no more.
issues.justification: Humorous doggerel; the 'Queen of Spades' couplet is rhymed but this one loses the original 'Съели оба те котлеты, нет Ромео, нет Джульеты' rhythm; the last line is clunky.

issues.source_quote: Вся Америка в страшном смятении. Эйзенхауэр болен войной.
issues.translation_quote: All America's in dreadful turmoil. Eisenhower is sick with war.
issues.justification: Velyurov's rhymed feuilleton loses all rhyme and doggerel humor, which is essential to the parody of Soviet agitprop.

issues.source_quote: Дорогу осилит идущий.
issues.translation_quote: The road yields to the one who walks it.
issues.justification: Established proverb ('The road is mastered by those who walk it'); rendering is awkward.

issues.source_quote: Поэтом можешь ты не быть, но гражданином быть обязан.
issues.translation_quote: "You need not be a poet, but a citizen you must be."
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the inverted syntax is a standard translation; fine.

issues.source_quote: Эмиль Золя угорел.
issues.translation_quote: Émile Zola died of carbon monoxide.
issues.justification: The joke (an in-house reply about poets dying) is retained, but 'угорел' (suffered carbon monoxide poisoning) is reasonable; however 'угорел' here echoes the series of dead authors and should convey the same dark joke.

issues.source_quote: Что-то вот у нас как-то сыро.
issues.translation_quote: It's rather damp in here somehow.
issues.justification: Euphemism for wanting a drink is lost; also 'Вы такой одинокий?' / 'Moments' register is formal.

issues.source_quote: Кулинар!
issues.translation_quote: Some chef!
issues.justification: Tone shift; 'Кулинар' is a jocular call, 'Some chef!' implies sarcasm.

issues.source_quote: Соблаговолите оставить номер.
issues.translation_quote: Kindly leave your number.
issues.justification: Acceptable; but 'Sehr gut', 'Danke schön', 'Jawohl' keep German while Russian flavor of Savva's comic German is mostly retained — fine.

issues.source_quote: Моя тетушка. Иду...
issues.translation_quote: My aunt. Coming...
issues.justification: Minor: 'Иду' is spoken to the phone ringing; fine but unclear.

issues.source_quote: Шекспир тоже переделывал старинные сюжеты!
issues.translation_quote: Shakespeare also reworked old plots!
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Я раньше эстрадным сатириком был... Громил поджигателей' is rendered with 'trounced', not capturing the doggerel meter.

issues.source_quote: Мастер спорта. Прекрасно плавает на спине.
issues.translation_quote: Master of Sport. Swims beautifully on her back.
issues.justification: 'Master of Sport' is a Soviet rank and acceptable, but earlier 'одну так недавно кинули' is mistranslated as 'someone threw her in' (should be abandoned/stood up or dropped), and 'Вы видите, дом наконец приобрел настоящего мужчину' shifts register.

issues.source_quote: Благодарю вас... О, благодарю... Мне было так хорошо...
issues.translation_quote: Thank you... Oh, thank you... I felt so good...
issues.justification: The speaker's names/pronouns and gender (nurse and Khobotov) are ambiguous in the target, and the comic innuendo of the scene is flattened.

issues.source_quote: Лев Евгеньевич, вы в цейтноте, в цейтноте.
issues.translation_quote: Lev Yevgenyevich, you're in time trouble, time trouble.
issues.justification: Chess term; 'time trouble' is correct but the metaphor is unclear without context.

issues.source_quote: Физкульт-привет!
issues.translation_quote: Sporting greetings!
issues.justification: Soviet greeting catchphrase 'Fizkult-privet' is rendered neutrally, losing period feel.

issues.source_quote: Нет, моя радость, я его отчим.
issues.translation_quote: No, my joy, I'm his stepfather.
issues.justification: 'My joy' is a literal calque; 'my dear' would sound natural.

issues.source_quote: Ага, отчим, щас. Так я тебе и поверила.
issues.translation_quote: Yeah, stepfather, right. Like I'd believe you.
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Секундочку, сейчас.
issues.translation_quote: One second, just a moment.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Вонзил кинжал убийца нечестивый в грудь деларю. Тот, шляпу сняв, сказал ему учтиво: благодарю!
issues.translation_quote: The impious assassin plunged his dagger into De la Rue's breast. He, doffing his hat, said to him politely: thank you!
issues.justification: The Kozma Prutkov-style parody depends on the comic rhyme 'деларю / благодарю' and on the absurd politeness of the victim. The English keeps neither the rhyme nor the doggerel rhythm, and the joke does not register.

issues.source_quote: В непосредственной близости от Покровских ворот.
issues.translation_quote: In the immediate vicinity of the Pokrov Gate.
issues.justification: The established English form is 'Pokrovsky Gate' (Pokrovskie Vorota), which is also the film's title. 'Pokrov Gate' is an unidiomatic rendering of the place name.

issues.source_quote: Я похож на какого-то стилягу.
issues.translation_quote: I look like some kind of hipster.
issues.justification: 'Stilyaga' is a specific 1950s Soviet subculture. 'Hipster' is a modern term and breaks the 1950s feel.

issues.source_quote: Шевелюров! Это звучней, к тому же менее мануфактурно.
issues.translation_quote: Velyurov. Chevelurov! More sonorous, and it sounds less like a fabric shop.
issues.justification: The joke turns on 'велюр' (velour, a fabric) versus 'шевелюра' (a head of hair). The English 'Chevelurov' and 'fabric shop' do not signal the velvet or hair link, so the wordplay is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Он, как человек ярко окрашенный, он по-своему привлекателен.
issues.translation_quote: He, as a brightly colored person, is attractive in his own way.
issues.justification: 'Brightly colored person' is a literal calque. In English it reads as strange and unclear, where 'colorful character' would be natural.

issues.source_quote: Вместо этого стал каким-то блохоискателем. Сундуком.
issues.translation_quote: Instead I've become some kind of nitpicker. A filing cabinet.
issues.justification: The self-deprecating imagery is flattened. 'Блохоискатель' (flea-hunter) is a vivid, comic word, and 'сундук' (a stuffy old trunk) is not quite a filing cabinet.

issues.source_quote: Невропат. Люблю ее! ... Сексуальный маньяк.
issues.translation_quote: Neuropath. ... Sex maniac.
issues.justification: 'Neuropath' is a rare clinical term in English, and 'sex maniac' is stiff. Margarita's dismissive medicalizing insults need more natural spoken English equivalents.

issues.source_quote: Но как вы спелись!
issues.translation_quote: My, how you two sing in harmony!
issues.justification: 'Спеться' here means to get thick together or conspire. The literal musical image reads oddly, and the ironic reproach is lost.
